findings.statement: A standard education and coarse experience-proxy association predicts upper within-country earnings ranks better than countryprevalence and comparably to flexible controls.

reliability.rationale: The standard education/experience-proxy baseline reaches Brier0.18202 versus country prevalence0.21941 and flexible0.18365. Its small flexible margin and source-aware cross-section support a descriptive reproduction.

mechanism.rationale: Upper within-country earnings rank is not a log-wage endpoint. Coarse age-derived experience, suppressed wages and plausible values conditioned on background preclude individual skill returns and causal education coefficients.

novelty.rationale: Known source analyses and standard mathematical/statistical families are disclosed. This review does not certify a new law or exhaustive novelty.

significance.rationale: Strong data-semantics example: excluding plausible-value leakage is more valuable than manufacturing a skill-wage discovery.

reproducibility.rationale: Native adapter, frozen equations, coefficients and compact evidence were inspected. Separate computational review performs numerical replay; scientific review is not experimental replication.

impact.rationale: No independent deployed intervention, measured cost benefit or external experimental replication establishes industrial impact.
